title: Messi Has 19 World Cup Goals, a Record No One Else Has Held, and Maybe Two Weeks Left. Cape Verde Stand in His Way.
excerpt: The 39-year-old is the all-time leading scorer in World Cup history. On Friday night in Miami, the smallest nation ever to play a knockout match will try to end his farewell tour.
body:
Lionel Messi turns 39 next month. He has played in six World Cups. He has scored 19 goals in the tournament — more than any man in history. And on Friday evening in Miami, in front of a crowd that will almost certainly include thousands of Argentine-Americans and a sizable Indian diaspora that has adopted him as a sporting demigod, he will take the field against the smallest nation ever to play a World Cup knockout match.

Cape Verde, population 600,000, has no business being here. And yet here they are.

## The Record Books Keep Rewriting Themselves

Messi's hat-trick against Algeria in Argentina's group opener pushed him past Miroslav Klose's all-time record of 16 World Cup goals. A brace against Austria took him to 18. A further goal against Jordan in the final group game made it 19 from 29 World Cup appearances. France's Kylian Mbappé, with 18 goals of his own, is the only player within range — and at 27, he has time.

Messi does not.

"For me, the main thing is to enjoy Leo Messi every single day, just as every Argentinian citizen," said midfielder Rodrigo De Paul, his Inter Miami teammate and self-appointed bodyguard on the pitch. "Of course, we always value those things more that we don't have anymore. That's part of life. But we are all enjoying having him around."

De Paul's words carry a particular weight. This is likely Messi's farewell tour. Every match could be his last in the blue and white. The Argentine squad knows it. The fans in the stands know it. And the 39-year-old himself, who has given few interviews about retirement, plays with the urgency of a man who understands what's at stake.

## Cape Verde's Cinderella Run

Argentina's opponents have earned every second of this spotlight. Cape Verde entered Group H as the tournament's biggest underdogs and walked out having drawn Spain goalless, conceded zero goals in three matches, and advanced as one of the best third-placed teams.

Their 40-year-old goalkeeper Vozinha has been a revelation. Their organisation under coach Bubista has been meticulous. Their president, José Maria Neves, predicted a 1-0 victory over Argentina and declared his team has "100% faith, 100% hope."

"We went to this World Cup to write our own destiny," Neves told the BBC. "We are going to face Argentina and Messi with the same determination, same will, and with a desire to win and reach the next phase."

It is a romantic storyline. It is also probably going to end on Friday.

## Scaloni's Squad Is Fully Loaded

Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni rested most of his starters in the dead-rubber victory over Jordan. Cristian Romero returns from a minor knee complaint. Julián Álvarez, fully recovered from an ankle injury, will partner Messi up front — the same partnership that delivered the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

The likely lineup: Emiliano Martínez; Molina, Romero, Lisandro Martínez, Medina; De Paul, Mac Allister, Fernández, Almada; Messi, Álvarez. It is, by any measure, one of the strongest squads in the tournament.

## Why NRIs Should Care

Friday's match kicks off at 6 PM ET (3 PM Pacific) at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami — a city with one of the largest Indian-American communities on the East Coast. For NRIs across South Florida who have watched Messi weave magic for Inter Miami over the past two seasons, this is a home game in every sense.

Beyond geography, Messi is one of those rare athletes who transcends sport and country. In Indian homes from Edison to Fremont, from Plano to Atlanta, his World Cup journey has been followed with the same devotion as a cricket final. If this is the last chapter, it deserves to be witnessed live.

The winner faces the winner of Colombia vs Ghana, who play later Friday in Kansas City, in the Round of 16.
